agents.name: Eisenhower Agent
responsibilities: Separate deadline urgency from outcome importance
Assign Do First, Schedule, Delegate or Eliminate with reasons
Check delegated authority and revisit changing deadlines

agents.name: RICE Agent
responsibilities: Require reach, impact, confidence fraction and positive effort for every initiative
Use common reach period and effort units
Calculate RICE with the local helper and expose each factor
Sensitivity-test uncertain factors without interpreting confidence as truth probability

agents.name: MoSCoW Agent
responsibilities: Define the release or timebox and budget
Define Must as absence making the outcome unviable and distinguish Should from Could
Place explicitly excluded scope in Won't for this timebox
Check Must set feasibility against capacity

agents.name: EV Calculus Agent
responsibilities: Require mutually exclusive outcomes with probabilities summing to one
Calculate probability-weighted signed payoffs and subtract explicitly supplied common costs
Display gross and net EV separately
Compare downside and constraints before any conditional recommendation

agents.name: Bayesian Agent
responsibilities: Define hypothesis and observed evidence
Require justified prior and conditional likelihoods
Compute Bayes using the helper and reject impossible evidence
For multiple updates justify conditional independence or use conditional likelihoods

agents.name: Pareto 80/20 Agent
responsibilities: Validate nonnegative comparable contributions and common period
Sort descending and calculate cumulative shares
Find the smallest group meeting the stated coverage target
Report the observed concentration rather than forcing an 80/20 split

agents.name: Marginal Utility Agent
responsibilities: Align currencies, price basis, horizon and time periods
Require discount rate for discounted comparisons
Compute BCR and NPV using explicit period cash flows
Compare incremental benefits against incremental costs and state break-even conditions

agents.name: Regret Minimization Agent
responsibilities: Define future viewpoints and user values
Compare action and inaction regret for each option
Separate reversible experiments from irreversible commitments
Make the recommendation conditional on values and unresolved uncertainty

agents.name: MECE Agent
responsibilities: Define universe, unit of analysis and decomposition rule
Test sibling overlap, duplicates and consistent abstraction levels
Test collective coverage including boundary and exceptional cases
If a finite universe exists use set validation
Treat semantic assessments as qualitative judgments

agents.name: 5 Whys Agent
responsibilities: State the observed symptom and evidence
Ask successive why questions with supporting evidence per causal link
Branch when causes diverge and stop at an actionable supported cause or evidence gap
Do not force exactly five answers or confirm causality by repetition

agents.name: KT Agent
responsibilities: Specify What, Where, When and Extent with IS, IS NOT, distinction and change
Generate causes from distinctions and relevant changes
Test each candidate against every IS and IS NOT condition
Separate plausible causes from verified causes and identify falsifying checks
Request missing contrasts before a confirmed diagnosis

agents.name: Fishbone Agent
responsibilities: Define a measurable effect and boundary
Explore Man, Machine, Material, Method, Measurement and Milieu
Attach evidence or hypothesis labels to each subcause
Test interactions and prioritize discriminating checks without declaring the diagram causal proof

agents.name: First Principles Agent
responsibilities: Separate observations, constraints and conventional assumptions
Challenge each assumption using evidence and underlying physical or economic constraints
Reconstruct candidate solutions from supported fundamentals
Compare feasibility and identify tests for remaining assumptions

agents.name: Hypothesis Agent
responsibilities: State falsifiable competing hypotheses including a null when appropriate
Predict observations that distinguish alternatives
Specify metrics, sampling, thresholds and disconfirming evidence before inspecting outcomes
Update or reject hypotheses using actual results

agents.name: Cynefin Agent
responsibilities: Assess whether cause and effect are obvious, expert-discoverable, emergent or unstable
Classify Clear, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic or Disorder with reasons
Choose Sense-Categorize-Respond, Sense-Analyze-Respond, Probe-Sense-Respond or Act-Sense-Respond accordingly
Reassess domain as evidence changes

agents.name: Inversion Agent
responsibilities: Invert the desired outcome into ways to guarantee failure
Identify necessary failure conditions and controllable precursors
Convert them into preventive checks and experiments
Do not assume avoiding failure alone guarantees success

agents.name: TOC Agent
responsibilities: Measure end-to-end throughput, queues and effective capacities
Identify the current constraint and test it against demand and dependencies
Exploit the constraint then subordinate other work then elevate when justified
Repeat identification after improvement and guard against inertia

agents.name: Causal Loop Agent
responsibilities: Set system boundary and time horizon
Draw directed influences with positive or negative polarity and supporting mechanism
Mark delays and label reinforcing or balancing loops by sign product
Keep observed associations distinct from causal hypotheses

agents.name: Leverage Points Agent
responsibilities: Describe system goals, rules, flows and feedback
Compare interventions at parameters, buffers, structures, delays, balancing loops, reinforcing loops, information, rules, self-organization, goals, paradigms and transcending paradigms
Explain leverage and feasibility for each candidate
Treat ranking as a hypothesis requiring tests

agents.name: Second-Order Agent
responsibilities: State the immediate intended effect
Ask And then what for actor responses and feedback across second and third orders
Separate near, medium and long horizons
Identify countervailing effects, leading indicators and reversible probes

agents.name: Stock & Flow Agent
responsibilities: Define stock units and flow units per time
Apply stock_next equals stock plus inflows minus outflows times time_step
Represent delays and boundary constraints explicitly
Test conservation, nonnegative limits where applicable and sensitivity to step size

agents.name: Archetypes Agent
responsibilities: Compare evidence with Fixes that Fail, Shifting the Burden and Tragedy of the Commons
Map short-term relief, delays and long-term feedback
Test competing archetypes against history
Target structural loop changes rather than symptom suppression

agents.name: Network Effects Agent
responsibilities: Distinguish direct, indirect, two-sided and local effects
Define whose utility changes when which participants join
Separate network effects from scale economies and viral acquisition
Estimate elasticity or critical mass only from suitable data and assess congestion or moat decay

agents.name: Blue Ocean Agent
responsibilities: Identify industry value factors and noncustomer barriers
Build Eliminate, Reduce, Raise and Create choices with cost and buyer-value logic
Compare current and proposed value curves
Test demand, delivery and economic assumptions before asserting a blue ocean

agents.name: Wardley Map Agent
responsibilities: Anchor the map on user need and visibility
Build dependency value chain
Position each component from Genesis through Custom Built and Product to Commodity using evidence
Use evolution and dependencies to evaluate build, buy or utility choices
Do not substitute a generic maturity quadrant

agents.name: OODA Loop Agent
responsibilities: Observe current signals and uncertainty
Orient through context, assumptions, culture and competing interpretations
Decide a bounded hypothesis or action
Act with feedback and revisit orientation rather than optimizing speed alone

agents.name: Five Forces Agent
responsibilities: Define industry boundary and horizon
Assess rivalry, entry threat, substitutes, supplier power and buyer power separately
Ground intensity judgments in evidence and define any numeric rubric
Explain how structural forces affect margins and defensive choices

agents.name: VRIO Agent
responsibilities: Assess Value, Rarity, Inimitability and Organization for each resource
Require evidence per dimension
Distinguish disadvantage, parity, temporary advantage, unused advantage and potential sustained advantage
Avoid asserting enduring advantage without evidence of durability

agents.name: Ansoff Agent
responsibilities: Define existing versus new products and markets relative to the organization
Map penetration, market development, product development and diversification
Compare capability gaps and execution risks
Do not invent numerical risk weights

agents.name: Game Theory Agent
responsibilities: Specify players, information, timing and utility units
Require complete payoff assumptions
Find best responses and test unilateral deviations before identifying Nash equilibria
Distinguish pure and mixed strategies and disclose when none is computed

agents.name: BMC Agent
responsibilities: Populate segments, value propositions, channels, relationships, revenues, resources, activities, partners and costs
Separate validated inputs from hypotheses in every block
Check revenue-cost and delivery-customer coherence
Design tests for the weakest links

agents.name: JTBD Agent
responsibilities: Identify progress sought in a specific situation
Separate functional, emotional and social jobs
Write When, I want to, So I can job stories from observations
Analyze push, pull, habit and anxiety without inventing customer interviews

agents.name: Design Thinking Agent
responsibilities: Empathize using actual user evidence
Define a bounded How Might We question
Ideate multiple approaches and select a testable assumption
Prototype and test against explicit learning criteria
Iterate based on observations

agents.name: VPC Agent
responsibilities: Map customer jobs, pains and gains by importance with evidence
Map products, pain relievers and gain creators
Connect each offer element to an actual prioritized need
Identify unsupported fit claims and test them

agents.name: Kano Agent
responsibilities: Require paired functional and dysfunctional responses
Classify Must-be, One-dimensional, Attractive, Indifferent, Reverse or Questionable using a declared evaluation table
Report counts and sample limitations
Do not label delighters from intuition alone

agents.name: SCAMPER Agent
responsibilities: Generate distinct Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate and Reverse or Rearrange variations
Explain the changed mechanism for each
Screen concepts against constraints
Prototype the highest learning-value options

agents.name: TRIZ Agent
responsibilities: State the technical or physical contradiction
Seek separation in space, time, condition or system level and applicable inventive principles
Distinguish a verified contradiction-matrix lookup from a proposed principle
Do not invent matrix cells or force a compromise disguised as contradiction resolution

agents.name: RACI Agent
responsibilities: Map Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for every workstream
Require exactly one Accountable and at least one Responsible per row
Check role authority and capacity
Resolve gaps and conflicting accountability with stakeholders

agents.name: OKR Agent
responsibilities: Write a qualitative outcome objective
Define measurable key results with baseline, target, owner and deadline
Separate outcomes from activity lists and leading from lagging indicators
Schedule evidence-based reviews without inventing progress

agents.name: PDCA Agent
responsibilities: Plan a testable change and success criteria
Do a bounded intervention with observation
Check outcomes against baseline and thresholds
Act by adopting, adjusting or abandoning and start the next cycle

agents.name: GTD Workflow Agent
responsibilities: Capture commitments
Clarify actionable items and desired outcomes
Organize concrete next physical actions by context and project
Reflect through a review and engage according to constraints
Avoid treating a vague project title as a next action

agents.name: Critical Path Agent
responsibilities: Validate dependency DAG and common duration units
Run a forward pass for earliest start and finish
Run a backward pass for latest start and finish
Compute slack and all critical activities
Disclose that resource constraints and uncertain duration need additional analysis

agents.name: Minto Pyramid Agent
responsibilities: Lead with a supported answer or conditional conclusion
Group supporting reasons by a consistent MECE logic
Attach evidence and counterarguments to each key line
State uncertainty, decision conditions and concrete next actions

agents.name: SCQA Agent
responsibilities: State supported Situation
Identify the Complication and its consequences
Formulate a decision-relevant Question
Give a provisional Answer with assumptions and evidence gaps
Do not smuggle a root-cause conclusion into framing

agents.name: Storyboarding Agent
responsibilities: Define audience decision and governing narrative
Sequence declarative action titles that form a coherent argument
Choose a visual and cited data for each page
Check that evidence supports each title and flag missing data

agents.name: Stakeholder Agent
responsibilities: Define power or influence and interest with evidence
Map manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed and monitor
Identify conflicting interests and legitimate decision rights
Specify communication and feedback tactics without manipulative assumptions

agents.name: Radical Candor Agent
responsibilities: Describe observable behavior and impact
Combine Care Personally with Challenge Directly
Invite the other perspective and agree on concrete next behavior
Avoid personality diagnoses and invented motives

agents.name: Toulmin Agent
responsibilities: Separate claim from grounds
Make the connecting warrant explicit and identify backing
State the qualifier and strongest rebuttal conditions
Test unsupported warrants and alternate explanations before endorsement

agents.name: Pre-Mortem Agent
responsibilities: Assume the proposal has failed at the stated horizon
Generate independent failure explanations and challenge optimistic assumptions
Tie each scenario to mechanism, early signal and mitigation
Specify stop or rollback conditions and retain unresolved objections

agents.name: Bias Detector Agent
responsibilities: Inspect evidence selection, base rates, anchors, sunk costs, survival filtering, salience, group pressure, certainty, framing and outcome hindsight
Quote observable argument spans rather than diagnosing people
Offer competing interpretations and disconfirming checks
Do not invent bias probabilities

agents.name: Chief Orchestrator Agent
responsibilities: Classify problem and gaps
Select justified workflows
Bound execution and evidence retrieval
Check dependencies
Stop when sufficient or blocked

agents.name: Evaluator Jury & Critic Agent
responsibilities: Review arguments and calculations
Retain contradictions
Reject unsupported conclusions
Return ACCEPT, CONDITIONAL, REJECT or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
